utterances.text: I cannot comment on this because I wasn't aware of the whole procedure and I wasn't informed about this or whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have to correct the transcript at this point. It's on page 85, it's line 11. It says, a murder of a woman in labour, which does not show what I said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I think point taken. And it doesn't change a thing any way because we know exactly what the previous evidence was. So let's -- but thank you for pointing it out. I had it in my head too but go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I would like to know, Major Rutten, about the evacuation from the compound itself. I know that you and your soldiers were by the bus depot but you also testified about the fact that there were 4.000 people inside the Dutch compound itself. Who evacuated these people from the compound?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: In the late afternoon, the people -- the people were led from out of the compound and our superior, the Major Franken, said that it was on orders of the Serb soldiers, Serb commander, in fact, he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. But at one point, the refugees who were in the compound, inside the compound, passed the gate and were let out by the Dutch soldiers, isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did they continue observing what happened to those who had left the base?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: We tried throughout the 12th and the 13th to observe what was happening with the people, by sending jeeps with personnel on it, with it, to the direction of OP Papa and, in fact, Bratunac or Kladanj. But every time we sent our people along, they were excluded from the convoy that was moving, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I understand that, but, say, from the place where you stood in the bus depot to the compound, there are some 500 to 600 metres. Don't hold me to it, could be more, could be less, but that road, along that road, from one location to the other, were there any Dutch soldiers? Was anybody sent there to see what was going on?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: The moment you speak about is in the late afternoon, that were the last refugees on the 13th. All other refugees had left then already. These last ones were put up to the -- in fact, the last convoy, and we saw them leaving the gate. I personally had a talk with Major Franken about that because I asked him what we were doing, and what we could do at that point, and he said to him, it was -- and he said to me, it was discussed with the Serbian leaders.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We will get to that a little bit later. But let's analyse the situation. There is this area around the bus depot where the greatest number of refugees are, and then there is a separate location, which is the compound, where there are some 4.000 to 4.500 refugees. Did you wait for everybody from the bus depot to be evacuated before you started evacuating people from the compound or was it done simultaneously from both locations?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: At first -- at that time, that the 4.000 or 4.500 refugees from the compound were evacuated, by that time the bus remise was completely empty.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So is it your evidence, that until the area around the bus depot was fully vacated, the evacuation of the compound did not even start? Did I understand you well?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: Yes. It started shortly after that, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: After the evacuation from the bus depot was completed, and there was quite a number of Dutch soldiers present there, did these soldiers go back to the base?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: Some of them, and a certain part were along the line to the buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: That means that some of them remained there even though the evacuation from that area had been completed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: If you mean remained at the bus depot, that is not correct. They -- everyone of them was back on the compound again, and the -- a certain amount of soldiers was along the road or along the road to the gate, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. After all of the refugees were evacuated from both of those locations, whether we consider them to be one location or two locations, that's irrelevant, what happened to the remaining items? Let me put to you actually evidence given by a witness who testified here. The belongings of the refugees could be found anywhere, en route, somewhere on the road itself, they were spread out all over the compound. Would you say that this was a correct description of the compound, the road, all the way up to the bus depot, according to your recollections?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: Yes, that is a right description, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now let us turn to a different subject, which has to do with you finding those nine bodies. When you found the nine bodies on the meadow, according to your own account, you were together with your two colleagues. This is what you stated in your evidence and that can also be found in other documents. Those two colleagues were Koster and van Schaik; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In your statement, the debriefing to the Dutch royal army, which is 3D42, on page 2, sixth line from above, in the English version, you said that prior to arriving to that location, to the meadow, you saw a Muslim man fleeing from the area. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Naturally, you concluded that he was a Bosnian Muslim based on the fact that he was in civilian clothes; correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: However, that fact alone cannot fully assure you that he was a civilian. He could have also been a soldier dressed in civilian clothes, correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: Yeah, he could have been anything, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. Based on the statement you gave to the OTP, I took it that you arrived soon after these people were killed, and that you concluded that on the basis of the fact that the blood had not coagulated yet and that given the fact that it was over 30 degrees, there were no flies on their bodies, but regardless of that, you didn't hear any shots, you didn't hear anything on the basis of which you could have concluded that those people had been recently killed or when they were killed at all?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: No. But what you leave out is that I -- I checked the bodies, if there was someone alive, and I felt their pulses and their throats to check whether someone could have been alive and all the bodies were warm.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [In English] Well, it was intentionally actually because that was my next question. [Interpretation] So you approached the bodies and you checked for the vital signs. Did you move the bodies?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: No, I did not move the bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Since you didn't move them and according to your own testimony, those people were lying supine on their stomachs. Were you able to clearly see their faces?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: Most of them, yes, because the faces were lying to the -- either to the right-hand or to the left-hand side, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Was any of those faces familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: No, they were not familiar to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So you basically cannot say who those people were, based on any prior knowledge. You couldn't give us the names or any closer identifying fact?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, is it time to end for today?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think so. Major, I think you can have a well-deserved rest. We will continue on Monday morning. Madam Usher will escort you and please, my recommendation of yesterday not to contact or let anyone contact you on the matters that you're testifying upon. Have a nice weekend. In the meantime, there is one final housekeeping matter that I wish to address very, very short. We are aware of an additional request that was made by some of the Defence -- or one of the Defence teams on behalf of others, particularly, the Serbian components of the various Defence teams pointing out to us that the new year for the Serbian component is on the 13th and 14th of January. And there was specific requests, if possible, to start on the 17th, in order to give an opportunity to the Serbian components of the Defence teams to celebrate the new year with their respective families at home. We can't start on the 17th but we will start on the 16th -- we will start on the 10th as already pointed out, and then, in other words, we will sit on the 10th, 11th and 12th, and we'll try to have the 12th sitting in the morning, if we can. That would enable you to travel back home and be with your families on the 13th and 14th and 15th. So we will not sit on the 15th, but we will resume on the 16th. We can't resume on the 17th. So that's the position. So we'll resume after the Christmas recess on the 10th, sit 10th, 11th, 12th, and then again on the 16th instead of on the 15th. The 15th will be off, all right? Thank you. Have a nice weekend and see you Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 4th day of December, 2006, at 10:00 a.m. 20 21 22 23 24 25
